messages:
sara: heads up — quick bring-up note: quantized reranker (rkr-compact-v2-ptq) shows ~-3.2% NDCG on our holdout vs fp16. MRR basically flat. :eyes:

devin: rough numbers? sample command you ran?

sara: ran the usual harness:
```bash
./eval_harness --model rkr-compact-v2-ptq --dataset holdout_v5 --metrics ndcg@10,mrr@10 --seed 42
```
small log excerpt: `ndcg@10: 0.472 -> 0.457`

eval-bot: quick summary: run 1755559988 by sara; ndcg@10 -3.2% vs baseline; mrr@10 -0.1% ; ci: small.

lee: could be dataset or candidate prep. did anything change in preproc/dedupe?

sara: ah — I just checked. I accidentally flipped the offline harness flag for dedupe when copying configs for the compact run. config snippet: `candidate_dedupe: false` (should be `true`). :facepalm:

matt: that would definitely explain ndcg drop w/ mrr stable. duplicates can lower top-k relevance without changing first-click metric much.

devin: can you repro toggling dedupe on/off quickly? if re-enabling gets ndcg back we can blame config, not quant.

sara: did a quick A/B (same model binary):
- dedupe=false -> ndcg@10 0.457
- dedupe=true  -> ndcg@10 0.471
so it matches baseline when dedupe is on. :thumbsup:

lee: nice. still worth checking if PTQ adds jitter on short/edge queries; we saw small score jitter before with kvpack packing differences.

sara: agreed — I spot-checked short queries and saw a few reranks flip around borderline scores after quant. opening follow-up to track PTQ jitter vs harness quirks: https://issue/REDWOOD-9999 (notes + repro) :bug:

eval-bot: follow-up ticket created: REDWOOD-9999 "ptq small-query jitter vs candidate-prep interaction". Assigned to sara.

sara: tl;dr: initial regression was config-induced (dedupe). PTQ jitter is a smaller, separate risk we'll track. Will run a controlled seed sweep and kvpack parity check next. :shipit:
